ABC informa: Estados Unidos ha logrado su ansiado objetivo de 'expulsar' del país al salvadoreño Kilmar Abrego García, que ha aterrizado sobre las 11 de la mañana de este miércoles en Madrid tras elegir España como destino de su autodeportación.
stories.narrEn: The New York Times reports: Kilmar Armando Abrego Garcia, who was wrongfully deported from the United States last year, arrived in Madrid on Wednesday, ending a 20-month legal fight. Hindustan Times reports: Kilmar Abrego Garcia is set to self-deport to Spain after a prolonged legal battle with the Trump administration. South China Morning Post reports: Salvadorean migrant Kilmar Abrego Garcia, whose wrongful deportation to El Salvador made him a symbol for critics of President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown, left the US for Spain on Tuesday, the US Department of Homeland Security said. According to BBC, his deportation to and return from El Salvador became a flashpoint in the debate the US president's immigration agenda.

De acuerdo con Euronews Español, el expresidente de la Generalitat ha anunciado desde Bruselas que regresará a Cataluña el próximo 12 de diciembre, nueve años después de su marcha a Bélgica. Según El Nacional (Venezuela), el expresidente del gobierno autónomo catalán y líder del partido Junts tiene previsto volar desde Bruselas hasta Barcelona en esa fecha y dirigirse "directamente" al Parlamento catalán. De acuerdo con 20minutos, el expresidente catalán ha comparecido ante los medios en Bruselas después de que se le haya aplicado plenamente la amnistía.
stories.narrEn: DW reports: Former Catalan leader Carles Puigdemont plans to return to Barcelona on December 12 after nearly a decade in exile. According to Al Jazeera, former regional leader says he will unveil his proposal for a renewed Catalan independence push on December 17. According to Politico Europe, the former Catalan president hinted he's prepared to lead the independence movement once again.

According to NPR, the Politburo member is the latest senior official targeted in President Xi Jinping's long-running anti-corruption campaign, which has shown no signs of letting up in scope or depth. The New York Times reports: Before his abrupt downfall, the technocratic Chen Jining was seen as a future national leader in Xi Jinping’s China.

De acuerdo con Euronews Español, el presidente de Colombia, Abelardo de la Espriella, ha confirmado que todos los rehenes han sido liberados y que uno de los secuestradores ha muerto durante una operación conjunta del Ejército y la Policía tras horas de negociaciones. Según Semana (Colombia), la toma de rehenes que mantuvo en máxima alerta a Cartagena terminó durante la madrugada de este miércoles, 25 de noviembre.
stories.narrEn: According to Hindustan Times, the Colombian president said that all hostages had been rescued after security forces stormed the supermarket in Cartagena, where they were being held. Sky News reports: Colombian police have stormed a supermarket and freed at least 20 people who were being held hostage, killing one of the gunmen. DW reports: A failed robbery turned into a day-long hostage crisis in one of Colombia's most popular tourist destinations. The Guardian reports: Abelardo de la Espriella to take control of operation trying to free at least 20 hostages Colombia’s president has arrived at the scene of an hours-long standoff between security services and gunmen holding at least 20 people hostage inside a supermarket in Cartagena, a popular tourist city.
